sentences.text: Nelakurthy Jyothi vs E.Naresh Kumar on 10 April, 2024
Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Shameem Akther
M.A.C.M.A. No. 713 Of 2006
Judgment:

1. This Appeal is preferred against the Order and Decree dated 19.12.2005 in MVOP No. 276 of 2005 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-IV Additional District Judge Warangal (for short, 'the Tribunal'), wherein the Tribunal granted a compensation of Rs. 29,250/-
against the original claim of Rs.1,00,000/- against the respondent No. 1/owner of the vehicle.
2. Appellant herein is the petitioner-injured, filed a petition before the Tribunal, under Section 166(1)(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the Act') read with Rule 455 of the A.P. Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by her in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 28.11.2004.
3.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-IV Additional District Judge Warangal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case of the appellant/petitioner is that, on 24.10.2002, at about 6.00 p.m., while the appellant was traveling by Hero Honda Motor Cycle, as a pillion rider with her husband and her daughter Vaishnavi from Wardhannapet to Warangal, an auto rickshaw AP 36 U 3791 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed the Hero Honda Motor Cycle, as a result of which, the appellant fell down and sustained severe injuries.

Immediately, the appellant was shifted to Jaya Hospital, Hanamkonda where she was treated as an in-patient 2 Dr.SA, J from 28.11.2004 to 7.12.2004 wherein, she incurred huge amount towards medical expenses.

By the time of accident,
the appellant was doing tailoring work.

4. Respondent No. 1, owner of the crime vehicle, filed counter admitting that he is the owner of auto bearing No. AP 36 U 3791 but he denied that the accident occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle and contended that the age, avocation and monthly income and the claimant be put to strict proof.

He also contended that the aforesaid auto was insured with 2nd respondent under a policy bearing No. 550507/31/04/6701422 that was valid from 9.6.2004 to 8.6.2005, therefore, respondents 2 & 3 are libel to satisfy the claim.
5. Respondent No. 2, insurer of the crime vehicle, filed counter denying the occurrence of the accident, involvement of the appellant/petitioner and the injuries suffered by her.
It also denied the age, income, occupation and health condition of the appellant/petitioner on the date of the accident.

It further contended that the auto rickshaw AP 36 U 3791 has policy No. 6701422 for the period from 9.6.2004 to 8.6.2004 and that the said policy pertains to vehicle bearing registration No. AP 36 V 3791 and therefore, the auto rickshaw involved in the alleged accident is not the vehicle insured with it under the aforesaid policy.
That the auto rickshaw set up by the appellant/petitioner and the auto rickshaw in respect of which claim is made is different vehicle.
Thus denied its contractual and 3 Dr.SA, J statutory liability and it finally requested to dismissed the petition with costs.
6. Respondent No. 3 remained ex-parte.

7. The Tribunal, after framing the issues and, on consideration of the pleadings and evidence of the witnesses P.Ws.1 and 2 and the documents Exs. A1 to A5 and Ex. B1, granted compensation of Rs.
29,250/- with proportionate costs and interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till realization against first respondent/owner only.

8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, and dismissal of claim against R2 &
R3/insurers this appeal is preferred.

9. Though this matter underwent several adjournments and the matter was directed to be listed under the caption 'for orders', there is no representation on behalf of respondent Nos. 2 & 3, though notices are served on them.
In the circumstances, this appeal is taken up for disposal on merits.

10. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant contended that there is an error in the pleadings as well as in the criminal case record marked before the Tribunal and the owner has no other Auto except the Auto bearing No. AP 36 V 3791 i.e., ('V' by mistake, written in the pleadings and in the evidence as 'U') that the Tribunal ought to have appreciated that the Auto bearing No. AP 36 V 3791 is responsible for the accident and injuries sustained by the appellant/claimant and prayed this Court to fasten the liability against respondent Nos. 2 & 3/insurer and also contended that the 4 Dr.SA, J compensation of Rs. 29,250/- granted by the Tribunal is meager, unjust and prayed to enhance the same.
11. As seen from the entire evidence on record, the Auto bearing No. AP 36 U 3791 had caused grievous and simple injuries to the appellant/claimant.

The pleadings, the evidence on record, Ex.
A1 attested copy of FIR, and Ex. A3 attested copy of charge sheet, show that Auto bearing No. AP 36 U 3791 caused injuries to the appellant.
On perusal of Ex. B1- copy of Insurance Policy reveals that the owner of the Auto bearing No. AP 36 V 3791 is, one Mr. E. Naresh Kumar i.e., R1 herein.

While determining the issue, the Tribunal recorded that the petitioner filed a Xerox copy of insurance certificate with regard to Auto bearing No. AP 36 V 3791, no policy copy of Auto bearing No. AP 36 U 3791 is filed in this case.
It is relevant to state that neither respondent No. 1 nor any person from the Insurance Company was examined in this case.
Except marking of Ex. B1-copy of the insurance policy, no other document was marked on behalf of any of the respondents.

12. In view of the submissions put forth by the learned counsel for the appellant, and the material available on record, the points came up for determination are:
1. "Whether respondent No.1, Sri E. Naresh Kumar, has got any other Auto bearing No. AP 36 V 3791, which is covered under Ex. B-1 policy? and 5 Dr.SA, J 2.
Whether auto bearing No. AP 36 V 3791 caused accident and injuries to appellant?
3. Whether the appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?

sentences.text: As seen from the pleadings and the entire evidence on record, respondent No.1-E.Naresh Kumar is the owner of the auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 36U 3791.
Under Ex.B.1-copy of insurance policy, the name of the owner of the auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 36V 3791 is written as 'E.Naresh Kumar'.
Respondent No.1- E.Naresh Kumar filed counter in this case admitting the ownership of the auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 36U 3791.
He did not file the copy of insurance policy of the auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 36U 3791.
As per Ex.B.1-copy of insurance policy of the auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 36V 3791 is insured and there was valid insurance on the date of the accident
, it is in the name of respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 has not contended that he owns and possesses an auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 36V 3791.
As per the evidence on record, respondent No.1 has no other auto.
The circumstances of the case establish that E.Naresh Kumar-respondent No.1 has got only one auto rickshaw i.e., bearing No. AP 36V 3791.
In these circumstances, it established that the number of the auto in the case records is wrongly mentioned as 'AP 36U 3791' instead of 'AP 36V 3791'.
Since there is no much difference in the letters 'U' and 'V', the mistake occurred is not either willful or wanton.

Therefore, it cannot be held that respondent No.1 6 Dr.SA, J is not the owner of the auto rickshaw bearing No.AP 36V 3791 and the said auto did not cause accident and injuries to the appellant- claimant in the case.

The Tribunal ought to have appreciated the facts and circumstances and had condoned the mistake occurred in the writing of the number of the auto and tagged the liability against respondent Nos.2 and 3 , insurers along with respondent No.1-owner of the accident auto bearing No. AP 36V 3791.
14.
As far as the award of compensation is concerned, there is evidence that the appellant/claimant suffered fracture in her left clavicle and suffered simple injuries.

The Tribunal while dealing this issue had elaborately dealt with the same relying on the evidence of PW-1- claimant and PW-2- doctor and also relying on the medical record i.e., Ex. A2- attested copy of injuries certificate, Ex.
A4- discharge summary of Jaya Hospital Hanamkonda and ultimately assessed the compensation of Rs. 29,250/- on all scores, viewing it, the same is quite just and reasonable.
The Tribunal has also given elaborate reasons to award the said compensation and as such no other opinion can be substituted on this score.

15. In view of the above findings it can safely be concluded that the first respondent, being owner of Auto bearing No. AP 36 V 3791 i.e. Crime Auto and respondents 2 & 3 being its insurers are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs. 29,250/- with 7.5% interest to the appellant/petitioner from the date of filing of OP till the date of realization.
7
Dr. SA, J 16.
With the above observation and modification, this MACMA is allowed as indicated above.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
